provenance.notes: No third party: the two browsers talk to each other (WebRTC), the handshake goes through the application's own endpoints and store, the media through the application's own TURN relay when one is configured. There are no terms but the site's own, hence no limit and every right: a site tightens this policy with its own (its relay's capacity, say). The package asks no STUN server by default (stun_urls: []). A site that adds a public one - Google's stun.l.google.com:19302 is the usual example - uses a server whose operator publishes neither terms nor limits for it (none found on 2026-11-10): that use is the site's to judge, and should be declared in its own tightening.
